note: Ground truth for the coneflower. Ranges were written by Claude from the sources listed plus tolerances Claude chose; some numbers are the owner's decisions. They were written after the first four builds had been measured with earlier scripts, so they are not blind. The bloom-end check and the tiers were added after the independent review, I had already seen the old p90 results (3 of 4 builds ended near week 32), so the new end window is not blind either. Checks marked advisory are reported but never fail the gate: they rest on one photo or on a leaf reading that a photograph cannot confirm.

visual: Leaf colour: photographs measure hue 69 to 70, saturation 0.53 to 0.57 (Minnesota Wildflowers and Illinois Wildflowers leaf photographs, same measuring method each time).
First-year leaf outline: pointed oval, about 2.3 times as long as wide, upright (owner's nursery photograph). Not the cut, lobed leaf of an older plant.
Head from the side: egg-shaped cone, tan with a dark ring at its base, rays hanging steeply (Ozark Edge close-up).
Head from above: round cone with narrow rays radiating, gaps between them (Joshua Mayer photograph, Wikimedia Commons).
Winter: large dark seed heads on wiry stems, a low rosette of colored leaves, no dead leaves hanging on the stems.
